title: Frequency Response of Other Stages
intro: The same node-by-node method gives the speed of every other single-stage amplifier.

items: Source follower: the input capacitance is about CGD + CGS/(1 + gm*RL) (the bootstrapping effect reduces it). Its output impedance rises with frequency (it looks inductive), which can ring with a capacitive load. Bandwidth is typically high.
Common gate: the input pole at the source is 1/(gm^-1 * (CSB + CGS)): fast, because the input resistance is low. The output pole is at 1/[RD*(CL + CDB + CGD)].

Cascode: the Miller effect on M1 is small because M1's gain is only about -1 (gm1 * 1/gm2), so its Miller capacitance is 2*CGD1. The cascode therefore has a much higher bandwidth than a CS stage of equal gain. The pole at the node between M1 and M2 is at about gm2/(CGS2 + CSB2 + CDB1 + 2*CGD1).

Differential pair: the half-circuit gives the same poles as a CS stage with the same loading; with active loads, a 'mirror pole' appears at about gm3/(CGS3 + CGS4) (plus the junction capacitances there) at the diode-connected load node.

blocks.title: Cascode Miller
blocks.text: Two stages have the same gm. Stage A is a CS stage with gm*RD = 20. Stage B is a cascode whose M1 sees a load of 1/gm2. Compare their Miller multiplications of CGD1.
solution: B: M1's gain is -gm1 / gm2 = -1, so the factor is 1 + 1 = 2.
The cascode's input Miller capacitance is about ten times smaller.
